articles.title: Learn Yjs and Building Realtime Collaborative Apps in JavaScript
articles.description: Yjs is a CRDT (Conflict-free replicated data type) library for building collaborative and local-first apps. CDRTs are powerful but can be tricky to ‘get’ which is why this new interactive Yjs tutorial is so valuable. A great way to learn about building collaborative, syncing webapps from the ground up.
articles.author: Jamsocket

articles.title: Bun v1.1.44: The Fast JS Runtime Adds On-Demand Frontend Bundling
articles.description: The popular, high-performance alternative JavaScript runtime has extended its Bun.serve() HTTP handler with support for bundling frontend apps on demand using HTML imports.
articles.author: Ben Grant

articles.title: A Checklist for Your tsconfig.json
articles.description: What I love about Dr. Axel is when he’s done the hard work of figuring something out for himself, he writes it down. So it goes here, with his journey to set up a good tsconfig.json for his projects.
articles.author: Dr. Axel Rauschmayer

articles.title: A Look at Regular Expression Pattern Modifiers
articles.description: You may be familiar with using flags to change the behavior of regexes, but Dr. Axel looks at a proposal bringing a way to change regex flags within subexpressions (e.g. /^[a-z](?-i:[a-z])$/i;). It’s at stage 4 and should land in ECMAScript 2025.
articles.author: Dr. Axel Rauschmayer

articles.title: Accessibility Essentials Every React JS Developer Should Know
articles.description: If you’re an experienced frontend developer, these might be second nature to you by now, but this is a good roundup of the entry level ‘table stakes’ for frontend accessibility, whether using React or not.
articles.author: Martijn Hols

articles.title: Five Years of React Native at Shopify
articles.description: Five years ago, Shopify said React Native was the future for mobile development at their company and they meant it, with every mobile app moving to RN over time. Here’s what they learnt along the way and why they’re sticking with it.
articles.author: Mustafa Ali (Shopify)

articles.title: Revealed: React's Experimental Animations API
articles.description: <ViewTransition /> is based on the browser's View Transition API. It’s only in pre-release versions of React, but Matt is armed with examples for you to get a feel for the potential.
articles.author: Matt Perry (Motion)

articles.title: ♟️ Chess.js: A Library to Manage a Chess Game
articles.description: Provides move generation, validation, piece placement, check/checkmate/stalemate detection – "everything but the AI!" v1.0 offers a rewrite to TypeScript and a variety of enhancements.
articles.author: Jeff Hlywa

articles.title: react-nil 2.0: A React 'Null Renderer'
articles.description: An interesting experiment to use React in situations where you don’t need it to render anything, but you want to use hooks, suspense, context, and other bits of the React lifecycle. Like in, say, a Node app. Maybe this CodeSandbox example will provoke some ideas.
articles.author: Poimandres

articles.title: 🔎 file-type 20.0: Detect the File Type of a File, Stream or Data
articles.description: For example, give it the raw data from a PNG file, and it’ll tell you it’s a PNG. Uses a ‘magic number’ approach so is targeted at non text-based formats. v20 adds support for yet more formats, including JARs, Word/Excel templates, and now supports ZIP decompression.
articles.author: Sindre Sorhus

articles.title: Node Web Audio API 1.0: A Web Audio API Implementation for Node
articles.description: More accurately, it’s a set of Node bindings for a Rust-powered non-browser implementation of the Web Audio API.
articles.author: IRCAM – Centre Pompidou

articles.description: The Angular team shares a brief update on how they're working on Angular's strategy for 2025.
👽 Alien Signals are coming to Vue 3.6... (it's basically a really fast way to handle signals.)
Tired of seeing this everywhere in your code? Dave Rupert has a fun way to turn it into a single glyph in VS Code.
Electron 34 – The JS, HTML and CSS desktop app framework updates to Chromium 132, Node 20.18.1, and adds a way to access the JavaScript call stack of unresponsive renderers.
Puppeteer 24 – Popular high-level API to control Chrome or Firefox.
Cypress 14 – Easy testing for anything that runs in a browser. Now supporting the latest versions of React, Angular, Svelte & Vite for component testing.
Storybook 8.5, ESLint 9.18.0, ESLint Config Inspector 1.0, AngularFire 19.0

articles.title: Six CSS Snippets Every Developer Should Know in 2025
articles.description: Adam shared a similar list last year and it proved incredibly popular — as such, he’s back again with another grab bag of hefty snippets which are “bigger, more powerful, and leverage progressive enhancement a bit more”.
articles.author: Adam Argyle

articles.title: ❤️ Top Pens of 2024 on CodePen
articles.description: Plenty of superb inspiration, demos, and neat tricks on show here. Whether that’s a neat parallax effect, a retro VHS look achieved with CSS, a rad web component that adds particles to your pointer, or this 3D image carousel. Lots of cool stuff to dig into.
articles.author: CodePen

articles.title: Cool People Link to Text Fragments
articles.description: Did you know that support for linking to text fragments is now enabled across all major browsers? It means you don’t need elements to have an ID in order to navigate to it, instead you can go directly to a specific text string. Chris briefly shows us how.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: The UX of Login Codes
articles.description: Brad explores the often very real friction that’s found between offering a great user experience and great security, along with the challenges and compromises that come with delivering both. “If your product texts/emails login codes, the experience better be amazing.”
articles.author: Brad Frost

articles.title: ▶  What is the Shared Storage API?
articles.description: Tara Agyemang from the Chrome team talks us through why we need shared storage, its privacy benefits, common use cases, and how we can use it.
articles.author: Chrome for Developers

articles.title: 'My Website Has Been Gaslighting You'
articles.description: Quite the provocative headline! Dave has been changing his site ever so slightly every day, tweaking the CSS by setting a --hue variable and rotating the hue about 1deg each day to make it 360º around a color wheel over the year. A fun little experiment.
articles.author: Dave Rupert

articles.title: Avoid Multiple Page Redirects: How Redirects Impact Page Speed
articles.description: Redirects add in steps that can delay page load, in-turn affecting user experience and Core Web Vitals results. As such, this post looks at how to optimize redirects to ensure faster browsing for visitors.
articles.author: Conor McCarthy

articles.title: Don’t Wrap Figure in a Link
articles.description: Highlights the inconsistent and problematic behaviours such as practice can inflict on voice control users.
articles.author: Adrian Roselli

articles.title: Shapecatcher: Draw the Unicode Character You Want
articles.description: Looking for a specific Unicode character, or just something close enough to represent what you want? This is pretty neat. Draw a shape in the box and you get the closest matches, ready to copy and paste.
articles.author: Benjamin Milde

articles.title: TailwindCSS Snippets: A Small Collection of Unique Tailwind Animations
articles.description: You can right-click each of the animations to copy the code or send the code to the official Tailwind playground, where you can live edit and customize as needed.
articles.author: Alexandru Ţurcanu

articles.title: Drupal CMS 1.0 Released
articles.description: The Drupal project is now 24 years old(!), and we now have two options for building with it — the original Core experience, or this new ready-to-use platform.
articles.author: Dries Buytaert

articles.title: Data Viz Project: A Huge Collection of Data Visualizations
articles.description: Mostly for inspiration or when you’re not sure what type of chart or graph to use. Currently includes more than 160 types of visualizations under 5 main ‘families’.
articles.author: Ferdio
